connections.why: Cell-membrane structure governs diffusion, osmosis and active transport
Mitosis must faithfully copy the cell's structures and DNA
Photosynthesis is the metabolic pathway that builds glucose using enzymes
Respiration provides the ATP that powers active transport
Exchange surfaces rely on diffusion across cell membranes
Leaves and the transport vessels supply and remove the reactants and products
Understanding pathogens and immunity underpins vaccines and antibiotics
Many diseases stem from lifestyle risk factors, not pathogens
The nervous system is one mechanism that keeps conditions stable
Hormones give slower, longer-lasting homeostatic control such as blood glucose
Nervous and hormonal systems coordinate the body on different timescales
Genes carried on chromosomes are passed on through meiosis
Inherited variation is the raw material natural selection acts on
Selective breeding and genetic engineering apply our understanding of variation
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that flows through every food web
Feeding relationships drive the cycling of carbon and nutrients
The web of feeding relationships underpins ecosystem biodiversity
Intensive food production must be balanced against biodiversity loss
Plant transport and growth limit the crop yields farmers can achieve
